claims.content: To enable a Customer Service Representative to resolve customer inquiries by investigating customer complaints/concerns and bidding issues using customer information and history.

goal.raw_text: To enable a Customer Service Representative to resolve customer inquiries by investigating customer complaints/concerns and bidding issues using customer information and history.

claims.content: Customer Service Representative
The Customer Service Representative has access to the Customer History Page.
The Customer Service Representative can access and edit customer information and research bidding issues.
A customer inquiry is received by Customer Service for resolution.

trigger.raw_text: A customer inquiry is received by Customer Service for resolution.

claims.content: The Customer Service Representative selects Customer History from the Administration Menu.
The Customer Service Representative uses the Customer History Page to aid in troubleshooting customer service issues.
The Customer Service Representative searches on customer e-mail address, phone number, or customer name.
The “Results:” section includes Last Name, First Name, City, ST, Zip, Phone, E-mail address.

If the Customer Service Representative uses the Bid History, Order History, or View Notes buttons on the Customer History Page, those buttons utilize anchor tags to take the user to the correct section further down the page.
The Customer Service Representative can use the Reset Password button on the Customer History Page.
If the Customer Service Representative chooses to suspend or deactivate an account, the Customer History Page allows accounts to be suspended or deactivated.
If the Customer Service Representative is deactivating an account, a supervisor's authorization code is required, and a pop-up DIV layer will appear asking for a supervisor's code.
If an auction participant becomes subject to the escalation policy for Review Status accounts, they cannot bid again until a Customer Service Rep removes the account from Review Status.

For a customer subject to the escalation policy for Review Status accounts, the only way for the customer to have their account removed from Review Status is by updating their account with a credit card; they may not use PayPal or Amazon Payments again until their order cancel rate falls below 10%.

If Amazon Payments and PayPal customers have a history of non-payment (whose auction orders are automatically cancelled after 7 days), they will be subjected to an escalation process; when these customers contact the call center, they will simply be reminded that winning incurs an obligation to pay.
If the account is deactivated, it will be listed in RED.
If the Method of Payment is credit card, the Method of Payment section (MOP) will only display the card type, expiration date, and last four digits.

1. If a customer inquiry requires the Customer Service Representative to place a bid for the customer, the Customer Service Representative can NOT place bids for customers. Exit: the bid is not placed by the Customer Service Representative.

2. If the Customer Service Representative chooses to deactivate an account, deactivating accounts will require a supervisor's authorization code, and a pop-up DIV layer will appear asking for a supervisor's code; a Customer Care manager will be required to approve, via code, a permanent suspension of bidding rights (“Deactivate an Account”). Exit: the deactivation is not authorized without the required supervisor/manager authorization code.

3. If an auction participant becomes subject to the escalation policy, they cannot bid again until a Customer Service Rep removes the account from Review Status; the only way for a customer to have their account removed from Review Status is by updating their account with a credit card, and they may not use PayPal or Amazon Payments again until their order cancel rate falls below 10%. Exit: the account remains in Review Status and cannot bid until the credit card update is completed and the order cancel rate condition is met.

4. If Amazon Payments and PayPal customers have a history of non-payment (whose auction orders are automatically cancelled after 7 days), they will be subjected to an escalation process; when these customers contact the call center, they will simply be reminded that winning incurs an obligation to pay. Exit: the customer is reminded that winning incurs an obligation to pay and remains subject to the escalation process.
The Customer Service Representative has handled customer complaints / concerns and researched bidding issues.
The Customer History Page has been used by the Customer Service Representative to aid in troubleshooting customer service issues.
Customer search results have been displayed with Last Name, First Name, City, ST, Zip, Phone, and E-mail address.

If an account was suspended or placed in Review Status, the customer can log in and change account settings, but may not bid, and the system will not generate orders for any auctions-in-progress that the customer may win.
If an account was deactivated, a supervisor's authorization code was required, and a pop-up DIV layer appeared asking for the supervisor's code.

If the account is in Review Status and subject to the escalation policy, the customer cannot bid again until a Customer Service Rep removes the account from Review Status; the only way to remove the account from Review Status is by updating the account with a credit card, and PayPal or Amazon Payments may not be used again until the order cancel rate falls below 10%.
